Today’s crypto policy conversation is focused on one question:

Will the CLARITY Act reach a Senate vote before the August recess?

The legislation has already passed an important procedural stage.

On May 14, the Senate Banking Committee advanced the CLARITY Act by a bipartisan 15–9 vote, moving the bill toward consideration by the full Senate.

But Congress is no longer the only institution shaping the market.

The SEC and CFTC have already issued a joint framework that:

• separates digital commodities, stablecoins, digital tools, collectibles and digital securities
• explains how investment-contract rules may apply to crypto transactions
• addresses staking, mining, airdrops and wrapped assets
• begins clarifying the jurisdictional boundary between the two agencies

The SEC’s 2026 regulatory agenda also includes clearer rules for crypto capital formation, custody and trading tokenized securities onchain.

This creates two parallel tracks.

Legislation defines durable authority.

It can determine which regulator oversees which part of the market and create a framework that future administrations cannot easily reverse.

Rulemaking defines practical implementation.

It determines how companies register, how assets are classified, what disclosures are required and how existing law applies today.

The CLARITY Act remains important.

But the market is no longer waiting for one bill to begin changing.

Congress is designing the architecture.
Regulators are already building parts of the operating system.

🔔 Uniswap launches Earn with Morpho lending vaults 

⚠️ Earn is available through the Uniswap Web App and Wallet, extending the platform beyond token swaps and liquidity provision into onchain lending. Users can select a supported asset, choose an amount and authorize the deposit with one signature. Deposits then earn interest paid by borrowers across lending markets selected by the underlying vault. 

⚠️ Uniswap does not charge a separate fee for using Earn. However, depositors remain responsible for standard Ethereum transaction costs, which can make smaller positions less economical when network fees rise. Deposits appear alongside users’ other assets in the Uniswap portfolio interface. The dashboard displays the amount deposited, the current yield rate and total earnings, while recording deposits and withdrawals in the account’s activity history. 

🔖 Morpho supplies the permissionless lending infrastructure behind Earn, while Gauntlet curates the vaults and determines how deposits are distributed across eligible markets. Vault curation can reduce the need for depositors to compare individual lending pools, collateral types, and utilization rates. Gauntlet can set exposure limits and rebalance capital as market conditions change, but depositors still carry the risks associated with those allocation decisions.

A vulnerability in the web-based management interface of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to view sensitive information in clear text on an affected system.
This vulnerability is due to insufficient access control enforcement for specific template types that are not included in the encryption allowlist. A low-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability by viewing logs on the local system or on a remote logging server. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to view sensitive authentication credentials, which could lead to further compromise of network infrastructure and connected services.

Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability.
